translation_notes: Textbook trav_existence over two disjuncts: `any(graph.triples((None, OWL.imports, None))) or any(graph.triples((None, RDF.type, OWL.Ontology)))` -> `bool(m{ ?s owl:imports ?o }) or bool(m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology })`, per the stratum's own mapping. No .first()/.one() involved: the value of the matched triple is discarded, only existence matters.

The region reads the WHOLE graph (no subject/predicate argument to vary), so proving both `or` disjuncts true needs two distinct graphs, not two calls against one fixture: fixture.ttl carries the False case (neither pattern, plus neighbouring rdf:type/predicate triples that must not match), and driver.py builds two further graphs inline (owl:imports only; rdf:type owl:Ontology only) to show each disjunct fires independently.
Deliberately broke the translation (dropped the second disjunct) to confirm rdfeval check catches it: FAIL call[2].result: values differ (True vs False). Restored, check is green again.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two `any(graph.triples((...)))` disjuncts become two membership tests, `(None, OWL.imports, None) in graph or (None, RDF.type, OWL.Ontology) in graph`, on one line; the extracted header is kept byte for byte.

optimized.ldpy: the same two disjuncts as `bool(m{ ?s owl:imports ?o }(graph)) or bool(m{ ?s a owl:Ontology }(graph))`; `a` for rdf:type. `@graph graph` and the call suffix measure the same number of tokens here; the suffix keeps the region to one statement, as on the Python side.

No exception to the symmetry rule. m{ } has no union, so the two disjuncts stay two islands, as the Python side keeps two tests. The notation ratio is above 1 because the three @prefix lines of the translated header (kept byte for byte) count against the ldpy side; the region line itself is shorter than its Python counterpart.
